summary: Forge 0.4.0 has 293 node:test cases across 13 files (75 adversarial, 45 auth, 30 envelope, 23 capture.full, 21 runner, 19 journal, 16 budget, 16 ui, 13 captures, 9 reconcile, 9 client, 9 release_loader, 8 harvest) built on four socket-free doubles: MemoryStorage/fakeClock (shim.mjs), FakeGame/FakeClient (fakegame.mjs), composeForTest wrapping the shipped compose() (compose.mjs), fake-indexeddb, plus jsdom for ~31 DOM tests and 11 recorded tRPC envelope fixtures derived by running real @trpc 11.18.0 in-process. Coverage is deep on storage/journal invariants, crash-resume/reconciliation, budget, auth gating, full-capture persistence and harvest.py agreement (7 tests shell out to the real script), and thin on UI (textContent regexes only, several buttons never clicked), zero on Uploader and Github modules, zero on accessibility/keyboard/responsive/visual/bundle-size. `cd forge && npm test` on this checkout (forge/ identical to main 305a28f) gives 293 tests, 292 pass, 1 fail, exit 1 in 10.2 s: release_loader.test.mjs:47 demands a @x-release-pending marker that the release-pin bot removed from main (d1dbecc), and forge.yml never ran on that bot commit (last main run #27 at ce603def), so main is red without CI noticing. forge.yml proves npm ci/audit/test, fixture reproducibility and bundle reproducibility on Node 24 for paths under forge/**, bundle, loader, harvest.py and pin scripts, but not for push/** manifests the suite depends on, not fields.json/nested.json regeneration, not the post-pin tree, and nothing about browsers. A UI-contract layer for Forge Next should stay in node:test+jsdom (serialized-DOM snapshots per screen×state, state-machine enumeration over the pinned journal transitions, axe + KeyboardEvent dispatch, awaiting promises instead of setTimeout), add runner-level tests through the real TrpcClient with recorded fixtures, and treat any Playwright/real-browser layer as a separate opt-in gate whose fake game is served by in-process route interception, subject to a user ruling on the socket-free rule.
